correctness.rationale: Away from the null set of planes through a vertex, section vertices are in bijection with crossed prism edges. The angle between endpoint vectors divided by pi is the crossing probability, by the uniform azimuth in their span. Summing one vertical edge per vertex and two horizontal edges per base edge gives the claimed normalization. Thin prisms have vanishing vertical angles and horizontal gaps summing to 2pi on each base. At large h the vertical angle is pi-2r_i/h+O(h^-3); for a horizontal edge the cross product of the scaled endpoints (v_i/h,1),(v_{i+1}/h,1) has norm e_i/h+O(h^-3) and their dot product is 1+O(h^-2), giving its angle e_i/h+O(h^-3). For a centered cyclic base put t=h/R, s_i=sin(delta_i/2) and c_i=cos(delta_i/2). The derivative has the sign of m-2 sum_i s_i t/sqrt(t^2+c_i^2); each summand is strictly increasing, so the sign function strictly decreases from m to m-per(K)/R. This covers the equality threshold too: the derivative stays positive at finite height. The strict bound sin(delta_i/2)>delta_i/pi gives per(K)>4R, and Jensen gives per(K)<=2mR sin(pi/m), proving the 3,4 and >=6 cases. The stated pentagon gaps tend to a perimeter of 4R, and interpolation with regular gaps stays strictly between 0 and pi, realizing the threshold. The regular-pentagon critical equation yields t=(3+sqrt(5))/4; independent evaluation gives mean 5.2462748197293845 in floating point, replayable with node /workspace/checks/geometry-and-word-reproduction.js. The universal conclusions follow analytically, not from sampling. The optimization is for centered cyclic bases, and h is half-height.

originality.rationale: Pass for the distinct general centered-cyclic perimeter transition, in particular the exact classification for nonregular pentagons. The angular expectation is an application of the standard spherical sign-crossing identity. Exact rectangular coverage is credited; the indexed later regular-prism record also matches the regular n>=5 formulas, including the golden-ratio optimum. The decision does not depend on treating either specialization or the general probabilistic identity as exclusively new.
residual_risks: The Shchur–Konstantinova paper was not available in full; its actual coverage is unresolved.

A general central spherical Crofton edge-sum statement or an older prism identity may already cover the expectation formula. The decision concerns the specific unequal-gap perimeter classification, not priority for the crossing identity or its regular and rectangular special cases.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural optimization question with one measurable base invariant rather than a numerical height search. In particular the number of sides alone does not decide the existence of an optimum at five sides: genuine centered cyclic pentagons fill both regimes and the boundary. This structural classification and its strictness are useful beyond the known regular or rectangular examples.
